product: Solid oxide fuel cell Energy Servers providing onsite electricity, plus installation, service and electricity contracts. Power Connect cuts onsite installation time by over 40% (2026-08-19) and an 800V DC-native architecture targets AI data centers (2026-09-16).
demand: Very strong and accelerating. Q2-26 revenue rose 165.5% and product revenue 215.4%, and full-year guidance was raised to $3.9-4.2B. Bloom says all major US hyperscalers and over a dozen US neoclouds, AI labs and colocation data center operators have validated and approved its power solutions.
pricing_power: Improving. Non-GAAP gross margin was 34.3% in Q2-26, up 604bps YoY, with product gross margin of 37.2% and full-year guidance of about 34%. Mizuho cited stronger pricing and demand signals. Pricing power is weakest in installation, which reported a negative 1.4% non-GAAP gross margin.
competition: Competes with combustion turbines, diesel gensets, grid supplied power, batteries and other fuel cell makers. Bloom claims it is becoming the standard for AI onsite power, citing an Oracle deployment delivered in 55 days versus a 90-day plan. Customer side project risk appeared with the Oracle force majeure notice on 2026-09-24.
team: Founder K.R. Sridhar is Chairman and CEO. Simon Edwards was appointed CFO (announced 2026-03-26), Aman Joshi is Chief Commercial Officer, and Shawn Soderberg is Chief Legal Officer. Bloom employs more than 2,000 people and manufactures its systems in the United States.
market_strategy: Standardize Bloom fuel cells as onsite power for AI factories through hyperscaler master agreements such as Oracle up to 2.8GW, capital partnerships such as the Brookfield $25B framework, and fast deployment products, while shifting installation toward a consult-only model for large load sites.
bull: Q2-26 revenue $1.0654B rose 165.5% with product revenue up 215.4%; FY26 guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B; non-GAAP gross margin up 604bps to 34.3%; Oracle master agreement up to 2.8GW and Brookfield framework expanded to $25B (2026-06-30).
bear: Oracle force majeure notice on Project Jupiter (2026-09-24) threatens flagship pipeline; Hunterbrook report and class action allege China scandium reliance; installation gross margin -1.4%; 63-day momentum -21% despite record results; forward PE near 100.
falsifier: Oracle terminates or formally suspends the Project Jupiter master agreement, or Bloom discloses a scandium supply disruption, on or before the Q3-2026 earnings call.
web_what_changed: Last 90 days: Brookfield power-financing framework expanded to $25B from $5B (2026-06-30); Q2 revenue $1.0654B, +165.5%, FY26 guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B (2026-07-28); Hunterbrook report and securities class action over alleged Chinese scandium reliance (2026-07-08); MiTAC expansion (2026-08-06); Power Connect launch (2026-08-19); S&P 500 inclusion effective 2026-09-21.
web_not_known_yesterday: 2026-09-24: Bloomberg reported Oracle sent a force majeure notice to Blue Owl, developer of the roughly $165B Project Jupiter AI data center in New Mexico, citing power and expense exposure. BE fell 3.1% to 266.65 while Oracle and Blue Owl also dropped. Not disclosed on Bloom IR site.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume-led with positive price and mix. Product revenue $935.4M rose 215.4% YoY on AI data center deployments while total revenue rose 165.5%. Non-GAAP gross margin improved 604bps to 34.3% and product margin reached 37.2%. Mizuho cited stronger pricing and demand signals (2026-09-14). Service and electricity revenue were roughly flat.
web_suppliers: Only evidenced supply issue is scandium oxide. Bloom said 2026-07-09 it has sufficient scandium, is not dependent on China, and has visibility to support 25GW of fuel cell output per year. Hunterbrook (2026-07-08) alleged sourcing through intermediaries from China, which a class action repeats. No named supplier list found.
web_customers: Concentrated in AI and hyperscale. Oracle master agreement covers up to 2.8GW with 1.2GW contracted (2026-04-13). Brookfield JV is a related party contributing $373.3M of Q1-2026 revenue but only $2.8M in Q2-2026; related-party receivables were $76.1M of $458.1M. Bloom says all major US hyperscalers approved its systems.
web_who_loses: Combustion and grid incumbents. Bloom states customers who traditionally defaulted to combustion technologies now choose Bloom, so gas turbine and diesel genset vendors lose share, as do utility interconnection dependent projects. Transformer and central power suppliers lose if 800V DC-native onsite power removes the need for transformers (2026-09-16).
web_contradicting_evidence: Oracle force majeure on Project Jupiter (2026-09-24) puts a flagship order pipeline at risk. Hunterbrook report (2026-07-08) and a securities class action with a 2026-09-28 lead plaintiff deadline allege undisclosed China scandium reliance. Installation gross margin remains negative at -1.4% non-GAAP in Q2-26. Stock momentum is -21% over 63 days despite record results, forward PE near 100.
web_if_management_right: FY2026 revenue reaches $3.9-4.2B, about 100% growth, with non-GAAP operating income of $800-900M, roughly 34% gross margin and positive operating cash flow. Capacity scales toward 25GW, Brookfield $25B finances projects, Bloom becomes the standard for AI onsite power, and orders such as Aligned Project Phoenix and MiTAC expansions convert into 2027 revenue.
web_if_management_wrong: Order and revenue timing breaks first. Project Jupiter force majeure delays or cancels booked GW, pushing product revenue right while inventory of $758.2M and contract assets of $365.5M sit unabsorbed. A scandium cost or availability shock raises product cost above the 36.5% product gross margin. Multiple compression follows because the stock discounts flawless execution.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Scandium and solid oxide ceramic supply chains, AI infrastructure financiers such as Brookfield and Blue Owl, natural gas fuel suppliers, 800V DC power distribution and electrical contractors, data center developers and hyperscalers needing fast time-to-power, and suppliers of fuel cell components, controls and installation labor.
